newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankrupt Berlin TV station announces layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Bankrupt Berlin TV station announces layoffs.

text.p: German regional television station Puls-TV, in the midst of bankruptcy proceedings, said on Friday it was laying off 64 employees and would let the last 60 go at the end of August.

Attorney Wolfgang Schroeder, who is overseeing the proceedings, said the channel will continue to be backed until end of August by newly founded station TV Berlin, owned by Thomas Kirch, son of media mogul Leo Kirch.

"With advisory and financial support of the Stadtfernsehen Produktionsgesellschaft mbH, which manages Thomas Kirch's TV Berlin, I will remain with the station until the foreseen deadline, August 31, 1997," Schroeder said.
Puls-TV, which serves Berlin and the surrounding state of Brandenburg, will show series and films in the meantime instead of its distinctive brand of home-grown programming, he said.
Last week Berlin-Brandenburg media authorities placed Puls-TV's frequency up for application and will decide on a recipient by August 15. TV Berlin is among the contenders.
Puls-TV declared bankruptcy in May after its investors, which had included Central European Media Enterprises, Time Warner Entertainment and George Soros, pulled their remaining funding.
They had said they could no longer carry Puls-TV's losses of nearly two million marks ($1.1 million) a month and were disappointed in the development of the Berlin television advertising market.

The channel was founded in 1993 and owners had invested about 130 million marks in it. But it failed in the ratings, never able to garner more than a one percent market share in Germany's competitive television market. ($ = 1.751 German Marks)
